title: AERCO BME: external interlock alarm
equipment: AERCO Benchmark boilers and BMS (Benchmark 5000-6000 manual cited; BMS has two interlocks that must both be closed)

n1.text: Record the exact alarm text, boiler tag, controller revision, operating state and BMS command. Is the alarm active, or latched/historical?

r_hist.cause: The alarm may only be a stored record or not cleared yet.
fix: Check the alarm history and how the manual says the alarm clears.
Confirm the interlock now responds correctly before clearing it.

n2.text: Using the unit-specific wiring diagram, is the interlock circuit in the state the manual requires under operating conditions? Continuity alone may not prove this.

r_trace.cause: The interlock circuit is open: a missing jumper, a unit disabled by the Energy Management System, or an unclosed proving switch.
fix: Check that a jumper is properly installed across the interlock terminals in the I/O box (if there are no external wires).
If external wires are on those terminals, check any Energy Management system or BMS to see whether it has the unit disabled.
Check that the proving switch for any device on the interlock circuit closes and that the device operates.

The manual allows a jumper to be installed temporarily to see whether the interlock circuit works. Only a qualified tech should do this, remove it afterwards, and never leave a safety interlock bypassed.
The Delayed Interlock is a separate circuit with its own message (DELAYED INTERLOCK OPEN) and terminals.

n3.text: Does the signal change correctly during the approved functional test, and do alarm history and related permissives match the manual?

r_cfg.cause: Wiring looks right, so a controller configuration problem is possible.
fix: Only if justified and authorized, back up the current parameter set first.
Follow the AERCO reset/restore procedure exactly and restore the approved configuration.
Field note: on BME boiler 2A, backing up and restoring parameters was followed by the alarms clearing. That is an observed sequence, not proof that a reset is the right first response.
Confirm the interlock responds, the alarm clears by the prescribed method and the boiler runs normally with all safety devices working.
